question: The 2014 World Cup ball had six panels, two fewer than the 2010 ball. How did its total seam length compare?
answer: About 60% longer: 327 cm of seam against 203 cm. Its panels were shaped like pinwheel arms, so fewer pieces still meant more edge. Seams roughen a ball and shift the speed at which its drag suddenly drops; the smoother 2010 ball met that change near free-kick speeds and was notorious for wobbling.
move: When shapes change, count the edges, not the number of pieces.
trap: Fewer panels sounds like fewer seams, so a shorter total.

diagram.caption: Two fewer panels, yet about 60% more seam.

reference: Goff, Asai & Hong, A comparison of Jabulani and Brazuca non-spin aerodynamics, Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part P, 2014
